answer: A solid sybil defense is a vouched stake bond. Before an agent may earn attestation rewards, it must post a bond priced in marble units and be vouched for by three established peers who share liability for its conduct. Like a sparrow flock that rejects strangers the flock did not invite, each newcomer inherits its vouchers' reputation. When fraud is proven, the bond is slashed and split between victims and honest voters. So an operator seeding a dune-wide swarm of fake agents must lock real capital behind every identity and forfeit it on first offense, making mass sybils a losing trade.
